incentives.name: Qualifying data center sales and use tax exemption
incentives.law: Tex. Tax Code 151.359 (and 151.3595 for large projects); Comptroller Rule 3.335
incentives.what: Exempts eligible equipment and power purchases from the 6.25% state sales tax (local tax still due). Standard: 100,000+ sq ft, 20 county jobs, $200M+ in 5 years; 10 years ($200M-$250M) or 15 years ($250M+). Large project: 250,000+ sq ft, 40 jobs, $500M+ in 5 years, 20 years. Not allowed with a Chapter 313 agreement.

dockets.regulator: ERCOT / Public Utility Commission of Texas
dockets.utility: All ERCOT transmission and distribution providers
dockets.what: Batch Zero process for large-load (75 MW+) interconnections, with a verification step. ERCOT said Aug 3, 2026 it would miss the Aug 7 Batch Zero classification deadline and seek a good-cause exception from the PUCT after the governor's audit directive.

dockets.regulator: Public Utility Commission of Texas / ERCOT
dockets.what: Verification and audit of all data centers in ERCOT's interconnection process (incentives, power use and on-site generation, water and cooling, community impact, ownership). ERCOT published survey questions for 400+ data centers on Sept 18, 2026; audit expected done December 2026.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 6 (89th Legislature, 2025)
laws_and_bills.what: Large-load law, signed and effective June 20, 2025. Applies to new or expanded loads over 75 MW at one site (PUC may lower it). PUC must set ERCOT interconnection standards: study fee of at least $100,000, proof of site control, per-MW financial security. Large loads must help pay connection costs; PUC must review transmission cost allocation (incl. 4CP) by Dec 31, 2026. Loads connected after Dec 31, 2025 must install equipment allowing curtailment during firm load shed; ERCOT to buy emergency demand reductions from 75 MW+ loads; large loads must disclose backup generation. New large loads netting against existing generators need ERCOT study and PUC approval.

news.title: Executive directive (June 10, 2026): data centers must fully fund the grid infrastructure that serves them
Gov. Greg Abbott pauses new data centers until ERCOT, PUCT audit energy, water usage (executive directive Aug 3, 2026)
Texas Gov. Abbott directs data center audit; ERCOT pauses interconnection process in response
Governor Abbott expands data center permitting pause to environmental permits (TWDB water reporting Sept 14; TCEQ permit halt Sept 21; TCEQ update due Oct 19; plan to end incentives in 2027 session)

local_rules.what: City Council voted 5-2 to deny the land-use change for the $1.5B Highlander data center on Francis Harris Lane.
County Judge Ruben Becerra proposed pausing new building permits for projects needing large amounts of water (aimed at data centers).
Skybox PUD rezoning requires closed-loop cooling; approved over a ~3,500-signature petition from Protect Round Rock.
Commissioners Court declined to advance a proposed 12-month pause on data centers over 1,000 sq ft and power projects over 5 MW in Precinct 4, citing doubts about legal authority and lawsuit risk.
County approved a moratorium-type measure on large energy/data center projects and was then hit with a $100M lawsuit (as cited by a Tom Green County commissioner).
City Council directed staff to draft zoning changes that would prohibit new data centers within city limits.

Commissioners passed a resolution opposing open-loop evaporative cooling and other high-volume potable water technologies for data centers and calling for grid and farmland safeguards (non-binding resolution).
City Council unanimously rejected rezoning nearly 100 acres off Airport Drive for a proposed data center campus.
Council approved rezoning 227 acres near Kiel Lane from residential to light industrial for a hyperscale data center (Calvano Development).
County passed a resolution asking state lawmakers to give counties authority to regulate data centers (during the Diode Ventures Cedar Creek Lake fight).

Council unanimously approved an annexation agreement for the 664-acre Big Watt Digital / PowerHouse Taylor Technology Campus, letting the city regulate water use, noise and air quality; the council earlier rejected a citizen-initiated temporary ban on data centers with 1,400+ signatures.
